title: Connect an agent and send an action
summary: Every agent gets its own key. It sends each action to AgentRaaS, which checks it, runs it once and records it.

dashboard: Click + Connect agent
Pick where the agent runs and give it a name
Click Connect, then copy its key and URL

cases.title: A normal call runs
cases.why: The key matches the agent, so the call is checked, sent to the payment API once and recorded.

cases.title: A wrong key is refused
cases.why: Nothing is sent. Check the key in Connect agent, or regenerate it.

response.error: Invalid or missing API key for this agent. Generate one from the dashboard's Connect Agent panel.

cases.title: A key can't act as another agent
cases.why: Each key belongs to one agent. The support agent's key is refused on the billing agent's URL.

response.error: Invalid or missing API key for this agent. Generate one from the dashboard's Connect Agent panel.

cases.title: An unknown action is refused
cases.why: Only actions the service has, or custom actions you registered, can run.

title: Safe retries (exactly once)
summary: An agent retries after a timeout, a crash or a loop. AgentRaaS recognises the same call and answers from its record, so the action runs once.

dashboard: Nothing to set up: every call is deduplicated
Monitor › Recent activity shows retries as deduplicated
notes: Same agent, same service and action, same payload = the same call
Or send x-agentraas-idempotency-key: one key per action, never reused for a different payload

cases.title: First call runs
cases.why: The call is new, so it runs and the result is stored.

cases.title: The retry is answered from the record
cases.why: "cached": true and the same payment id: the payment API was not called again.

cases.title: A different payload is a new call
cases.why: Another amount is another action, so it runs.

cases.title: Your own idempotency key
cases.why: With x-agentraas-idempotency-key you name the action yourself, for example by your order id.

cases.title: Same key, same body: answered from the record
cases.why: The retry carries the same key, so it is the same action.

cases.title: Same key, different body: refused
cases.why: A key stands for one exact action. Reusing it for something else is a bug in the caller, so it gets 422 and nothing runs.

response.error: This Idempotency-Key was already used with a different payload. Use a new key for a different request.

title: Validation rules
summary: Check every payload before it is sent. A call that breaks a rule is refused with 422, nothing reaches the provider, and the answer tells the agent how to fix it.

dashboard: Rules › Validation rules
Pick the service and action
Add a rule per field: type, min, max, or not more than another field

rules.label: amount: a number from 100 to 10000, never above balance

cases.title: A good payload runs
cases.why: Every field passes.

cases.title: Too big
cases.why: Above max: refused, nothing sent.

validation_errors.hint: Use a value of 10000 or less for "amount".

response.next_step: Nothing was sent. Fix every field listed in validation_errors, following each hint, and send the call again.

cases.title: Too small
cases.why: Below min.

validation_errors.hint: Use a value of 100 or more for "amount".

response.next_step: Nothing was sent. Fix every field listed in validation_errors, following each hint, and send the call again.

cases.title: Wrong type
cases.why: A string where a number belongs. The hint says what to send instead.

response.error: amount must be number, got string

validation_errors.message: amount must be number, got string

response.next_step: Nothing was sent. Fix every field listed in validation_errors, following each hint, and send the call again.

cases.title: More than the balance
cases.why: amount may not be above the payload's own balance field.

validation_errors.hint: Lower "amount" to 2000 or less, the current "balance".

response.next_step: Nothing was sent. Fix every field listed in validation_errors, following each hint, and send the call again.

title: Human approval
summary: Hold risky calls until a person says yes. The agent gets 202 and a status URL; the call runs once when approved, or never when denied.

dashboard: Rules › Approval rules
Pick the service and action
Optional: only when a field passes a threshold (amount > 5000)
Approve in Monitor › Waiting for approval, Slack, Teams, Telegram, Discord, email, or agtrs approve

cases.title: Under the threshold runs at once
cases.why: amount 3000 is not above 5000, so no approval is needed.

cases.title: Over the threshold is held
cases.why: The agent gets 202 and a status URL. Nothing has run yet.

cases.title: A retry while it waits is not a second request
cases.why: The same call again gets 409 until someone decides.

response.error: An identical request is already being processed. Retry shortly.

cases.title: Approve: the call runs once
cases.why: In the dashboard, Slack, an approval link, or agtrs approve. The held call runs now.

cases.title: The agent checks its status URL
cases.why: The status URL now carries the result.

cases.title: Another big charge is held
cases.why: A second request over the threshold.

cases.title: Deny: it never runs
cases.why: The call is dropped. Nothing reaches the payment API.

cases.title: The status URL says denied
cases.why: The agent can stop or ask for a smaller amount.

title: Spend caps and money caps
summary: Limit how often an agent may act, or how much money it may move per day. Over the limit, the call is refused (429) or held for approval.

dashboard: Rules › Spend caps
Count calls (max calls per hour or day), or add up a money field (max amount per day, in your time zone)
Over the limit: block, or hold for approval

rules.label: billing-agent: at most 2 payments an hour
all agents: at most 10000 in amount per day (Asia/Kolkata)
support-agent: 1 payment an hour, then ask a person

cases.title: Call 1 of 2 runs
cases.why: Inside the limit.

cases.title: Call 2 of 2 runs
cases.why: Still inside.

cases.title: Call 3 is refused
cases.why: The cap is reached: 429, nothing sent, until the hour rolls over.

response.error: Spend cap exceeded for mockpay.payment.create: 3/2 calls this hour (rule #284).

cases.title: Other agents are not affected
cases.why: The cap names billing-agent, so the support agent's call runs.

cases.title: A money cap adds up the amounts
cases.why: 6000 of the 10000 for today.

cases.title: Going over the daily total is refused
cases.why: 6000 + 5000 would be 11000, above 10000. The refused call uses none of the budget.

response.error: Spend cap exceeded for mockpay.payment.create: amount 5000 would bring this day's total to 11000, above 10000 (rule #285).

cases.title: Inside the cap runs
cases.why: First payment this hour.

cases.title: Over the cap waits for a person
cases.why: on_exceed hitl: held for approval instead of refused.

Pick an agent (or all), a service and an action (* for every action)
Effect: deny, or require fields / hours

title: Failures and the dead-letter queue
summary: When the provider fails, the agent gets the error and the call is kept in the dead-letter queue, with its payload, to replay later. Nothing is silently lost.

dashboard: Monitor › Failed requests lists every call that failed
Replay sends it again with the same Idempotency-Key, so it still runs at most once

cases.title: The provider fails
cases.why: mockpay with fail: true always errors (it stands in for a provider outage). The agent gets the error.

cases.title: It is in the dead-letter queue
cases.why: Monitor › Failed requests, or the API, lists it with the error.

cases.title: Replay it
cases.why: Sent again with the same Idempotency-Key, so it still runs at most once. This payload still says fail: true, so it fails again ("replayed": false); once a real provider is back, the replay runs it.

cases.title: Repeated failures open the circuit breaker
cases.why: Calls to mockpay now get 503 at once, without being sent, so a broken provider is not hammered and the agent can back off.

response.error: Circuit breaker open for mockpay. Try again later.

cases.title: After 30 seconds, one call is let through
cases.why: It works, so the breaker closes and calls flow again.

cases.title: Back to normal
cases.why: The next call runs as usual.

title: Undo an action
summary: Reverse something an agent did: a charge is refunded, a Slack message deleted, your own action reversed by the action you named. Each one can be undone once, for 30 days.

dashboard: Monitor › Undo actions
Click Undo next to the action

cases.title: A charge runs
cases.why: It has a known reverse (payment.refund), so it is recorded as undoable.

cases.title: It appears in Undo actions
cases.why: With what undoing it will run.

cases.title: Undo: the charge is refunded
cases.why: The reverse runs once, with its own idempotency key.

cases.title: A second undo is refused
cases.why: Already undone: 409, the refund never runs twice.

response.error: Can't undo: this entry is undone.

title: Record and replay
summary: Record a run against the real providers once, then replay it in tests: every call is answered from the recording and nothing reaches the provider.

dashboard: Add X-AgentRaaS-Record: <name> to the calls of one run
Replay with X-AgentRaaS-Replay: <name> and a run id
Monitor › Recordings lists them
notes: Python: Client(..., record="refund-flow") or replay="refund-flow", run_id=...
JS: record / replay / runId in the Client options

cases.title: Record call 1
cases.why: Runs for real and is kept under the name checkout-flow.

cases.title: Record call 2
cases.why: Also kept, in order.

cases.title: Replay call 1
cases.why: Answered from the recording: same payment id, nothing sent.

cases.title: Replay call 2 with a changed payload
cases.why: Still answered, but payload_matches is false, so a test can fail on it.

cases.title: A call the recording does not have
cases.why: 404: the agent now makes more calls than it did when recorded.

response.error: Recording "checkout-flow" has no call #3 to mockpay.payment.create. The agent made a call the recording doesn't have.

title: Rules as code
summary: Keep rules in a YAML file in your repo, review changes like code, and apply them from CI. agentraas apply makes the server match the file; running it twice changes nothing.

env: AGENTRAAS_EMAIL / AGENTRAAS_PASSWORD: a user who can change the org

file.name: agentraas.yaml

cases.title: Preview the plan
cases.why: --dry-run prints what would change and changes nothing.
cases.output:
+ ValidationRule org_acme mockpay.payment.create (sane-amounts)
+ SpendCap org_acme mockpay.payment.refund (refund-budget)

cases.title: Apply it
cases.why: Creates what is missing.
cases.output:
+ ValidationRule org_acme mockpay.payment.create (sane-amounts)
+ SpendCap org_acme mockpay.payment.refund (refund-budget)

cases.title: Apply again: nothing to do
cases.why: The server already matches the file.

cases.title: Change a limit in the file
cases.why: max 10000 becomes 5000; apply replaces the rule that changed.

cases.title: Remove a rule with --prune
cases.why: Without --prune, rules missing from the file are left alone. With it, they are deleted.
cases.cmd: agtrs apply -f agentraas.yaml --prune   # after deleting the SpendCap from the file

cases.title: A mistake fails the CI job
cases.why: An unknown kind is reported and the command exits non-zero, so the pipeline stops.

cases.output: agentraas.yaml document 2: kind must be one of DedupRule, ValidationRule, ActionPolicy, SpendCap

title: Library mode and the chaos tester
summary: No server at all: a decorator makes a function with side effects run once, even when it is retried, and the chaos tester finds the calls that would run twice.

cases.title: Wrap a function: a retry runs it once
cases.why: The second call with the same arguments returns the stored result; the function body does not run.
cases.output:
charging cus_42 4200
ch_cus_42_4200
ch_cus_42_4200
  charging cus_42 900
ch_cus_42_900
times charged: 2

file.name: lib_demo.py
file.text:
from agentraas.local import exactly_once

calls = 0

@exactly_once()                 # state in a local SQLite file
def charge(customer, amount):
    global calls
    calls += 1
    print(f"  charging {customer} {amount}")
    return f"ch_{customer}_{amount}"

print(charge("cus_42", 4200))   # runs
print(charge("cus_42", 4200))   # retry: cached, no second charge
print(charge("cus_42", 900))    # different arguments: runs
print("times charged:", calls)

cases.title: A failure is not cached
cases.why: If the function raises, nothing is stored, so the retry runs for real.
cases.output:
failed: provider timed out (not cached, a retry runs again)
inv_cus_77
attempts: 2

file.name: err_demo.py

cases.title: The chaos tester finds a double charge
cases.why: It lets each write run, then drops the response. The agent retries without an idempotency key, and the charge runs twice.
cases.output:
agentraas-chaos listening on http://127.0.0.1:8787 -> mock (fault: lost-response)
agentraas-chaos: 2 write requests, 1 responses dropped after execution

  DUPLICATES: 1 action(s) executed more than once

    2x  POST /v1/charges  (body sha256 a32934913660)

  Fix: send an Idempotency-Key header that stays the same across retries, for
  providers that honor one. With agentraas.local.exactly_once, give the function an
  `idempotency_key` parameter and send it as that header; for providers without
  idempotency support, route the call through an AgentRaaS server.

file.name: agent.py

cases.title: With exactly_once and an idempotency key it passes
cases.why: The retry carries the same key, so nothing doubles. Exit code 0, so CI passes.
cases.output:
agentraas-chaos listening on http://127.0.0.1:8787 -> mock (fault: lost-response)
agentraas-chaos: 2 write requests, 1 responses dropped after execution

  No duplicates: every retried write was deduplicated or never retried.

  Protected by an idempotency key: 1 retry

file.name: agent_fixed.py

title: LangChain and LangGraph tools
summary: Wrap the tools that have side effects. When the model calls one again with the same arguments, or the graph re-runs after a crash, the stored result comes back instead of a second action.

notes: CrewAI: from agentraas.crewai import protect_tool, same idea
Vercel AI SDK: protectTools in the npm package

cases.title: Protect a tool
cases.why: Use the protected tool wherever the agent takes its tools: create_react_agent, ToolNode, an AgentExecutor.
cases.output:
refund 1 sent to cus_9
refund 1 sent to cus_9
refund 2 sent to cus_9
refunds actually sent: 2

file.name: lc_demo.py
file.text:
from langchain_core.tools import tool
from agentraas.langchain import protect_tool

sent = []

@tool
def send_refund(customer: str, amount: int) -> str:
    """Refund a customer."""
    sent.append((customer, amount))
    return f"refund {len(sent)} sent to {customer}"

safe = protect_tool(send_refund)

print(safe.invoke({"customer": "cus_9", "amount": 500}))   # runs
print(safe.invoke({"customer": "cus_9", "amount": 500}))   # model repeats itself: stored result
print(safe.invoke({"customer": "cus_9", "amount": 700}))   # different arguments: runs
print("refunds actually sent:", len(sent))

title: MCP: scan and wrap a server
summary: agentraas scan lists which tools of an MCP server can move money, delete data or send messages. agentraas wrap puts exactly-once in front of the server, so a retrying or looping model cannot run the same write twice.
